page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-8 is a high-memory general compute instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting f, vnni, and bf16 vector operations), AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance contains zero local disk storage and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high single-threaded efficiency alongside standard multi-threaded throughput. In single-core stress-ng benchmarks, the instance recorded a score of 3,458.79, ranking in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded data handling tests also showed top-tier performance, with gzip compression registering 37.53 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 16.9 GB/sec. Multi-core performance aligns with standard 8-vCPU expectations, achieving 13,840.83 in multi-core stress-ng and 17,629.38 in the PassMark CPU test. Measured memory throughput reached 48.14 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 28.23 GB/sec for uncached writes.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory distribution, the n4d-highmem-8 delivers cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial RAM buffers without requiring higher core allocations. The absence of bundled local storage means persistence relies entirely on network-attached storage volumes, which introduces remote storage latency considerations. Network and memory operational benchmarks show 15.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 26.61 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Recommended workloads include Redis and Memcached caching tiers, relational database instances, ETL data pipelines, and memory-constrained application backends.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-8 is an AMD EPYC 9B45-powered virtual machine utilizing the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 64.0 GB of memory. Designed with an expanded 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, it features 32 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core CPU throughput, reaching 3,458.79 in stress-ng and 37.53 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, while multi-core compute and PassMark CPU metrics sit within the middle 50% tier. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for persistence. In-memory operations demonstrate solid execution with 15.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 48.14 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. This configuration is particularly suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, and web application servers requiring substantial working memory without excessive compute scaling.
